title: adaptive-slowdown-gate-batcher-queueing-to-protect-latency-sensitive-requests
author: Liam O'Connor
description:
Motivation: In production we observed recurring tail-latency outliers for latency-sensitive (short-seq) traffic that were correlated with long-running KV-heavy batches draining the continuous batcher. Existing fairness heuristics prevented total starvation but allowed multi-second tail regressions when a small number of pinned KV requests held slots for extended periods. This PR introduces an adaptive slowdown gate and light-weight preemption hints to the continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce head-of-line blocking while preserving throughput for KV workloads.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds an adaptive slowdown gating policy that probabilistically decelerates incoming large/kv-heavy requests when queue_age and active_slot_utilization exceed configured thresholds; introduces a per-class soft-reservation token bucket so short/low-token requests can reserve a small fraction of slots; exposes new metrics for class_starvation_rate and gate_activation_seconds; provides kernel-choice hinting to prefer small-batch kernels for latency-sensitive slots; and includes unit + integration tests and a micro-benchmark.

Key implementation notes: - scheduler/continuous_batcher: new gate "AdaptiveSlowdownGate" implementing a sliding-age window and exponential backoff for large request admission. Gate parameters are runtime-configurable via config/continuous_batcher.yaml. - scheduler/slot_reservation: adds ClassReservationManager (lightweight, lock-free signal with atomic counters) to allow short-seq and realtime classes to keep up to N reserved slots per worker. - runtime/kernel_hint: add hint_bytes and hint_seq_len to request metadata so the runtime chooses the small-batch kernel path when reservation assigned. - kv/cache: when a request is flagged kv-heavy + gated, the KV pinning path now returns a probe token that allows the scheduler to consider a preemptible state for long pins (reduces hold-time bias). - metrics: instrumented queue_age_histogram, per-class_p99_latency, gate_activation_seconds_total.

Why this is safe: The gate does not drop requests; it only delays admission (with jitter) and reduces the probability of starting large work when the continuous-batcher is under stress. Reservations are soft and bounded (configurable) so they cannot be abused by a single tenant. Kernel hints are advisory and fall back to default paths if unsupported. Changes include feature flags and staged rollout in console.

Benchmarks (micro-bench in CI/perf lab): baseline vs patch under mixed workload (70% short-seq, 30% kv-heavy large sequences): - p50 latency (short): 12ms -> 11ms (-8%) - p95 latency (short): 74ms -> 38ms (-49%) - p99 latency (short): 320ms -> 78ms (-76%) - throughput change (tokens/sec, aggregate): -2.3% (within SLO) - CPU/GPU utilization for KV-heavy flows increased slightly due to more efficient packing but overall cost per-token unchanged. Detailed raw bench output attached as commit notes.

Migration and rollout: Feature gated (continuous_batcher.adaptive_slowdown.enabled=false by default). Rollout plan: enable in canary cluster for 24h behind runtime flag, monitor per-class_starvation_rate and overall request success. If any degradation >5% on throughput we will rollback. Console exposes toggle and recommended config presets (balanced/latency-sensitive/kv-throughput).

Commits summary: - 1a3f4d2: initial AdaptiveSlowdownGate prototype + unit tests - 8b2e90c: ClassReservationManager implementation + metrics - d4fa7b1: kernel hint plumbing + small-batch kernel selection - e9b3c18: kv probe token & preemptible pin integration - f52c1a7: integration tests + perf harness + docs config snippet - 0c6a9e3: test flakiness fixes and CI perf stability tuning

Files changed (high-level): scheduler/continuous_batcher.go, scheduler/reservations.go, runtime/kernel_hint.go, runtime/kernel_selector.go, kv/pinner.go, config/continuous_batcher.yaml, metrics/collector.go, tests/batcher_integration_test.go, perf/bench_mixed_workload.py, docs/continuous_batcher.md

Review conversation (high-level excerpts): - Aisha Patel (reviewer): "Can we make the reservation limits tenant-scoped? Otherwise a noisy tenant could monopolize soft slots."  Author: "Reservations are soft and bounded by worker-global caps; updated comments + added tenant-scoped override with per-tenant caps via config. See reservations.go lines ~120." - Marco Alvarez (reviewer): "What about backpressure amplification when gate activation spikes? We should add jitter and an emergency bypass for critical system routes." Author: "Added jitter (0-10% of configured delay) and a bypass for routes marked system=true. Documented in config and tests included." - Priya Srinivasan (reviewer): "Please add a perf test that ramps to 95% slot utilization; previous fairness patches regressed there." Author: "Added bench_mixed_workload.py variant that drives utilization and included CI run results." - Evan Chu (approver): "Looks good after addressing comment about metrics cardinality. +1"

CI status and checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - linters: pass with minor style suggestions auto-fixed - perf/e2e-canary: perf harness run (attachments): stable; two outliers rerun and passed - security-scan: pass (no secrets)

Merge: squash-merge into main; changelog: documented under docs/continuous_batcher.md and release notes.

Notes for operators: - New config keys under continuous_batcher: adaptive_slowdown.enabled (bool), adaptive_slowdown.window_ms, adaptive_slowdown.threshold_active_slots, reservation.short_seq_slots_per_worker, gate.jitter_pct. - Recommended starting preset for latency-sensitive workloads: enabled=true, window_ms=250, threshold_active_slots=0.85, short_seq_slots_per_worker=2, gate.jitter_pct=8

Follow-ups: - Expose gate metrics to Console breakout by route/token to allow per-route tuning (ENG-4317) - Evaluate adding a learning-based admission predictor once we have more production signal (ENG-4391)

release_notes: Adaptive slowdown gate for continuous batcher: reduces p99 tail for short-sequence requests under mixed KV-heavy workloads; feature-flagged and configurable.
